comparison: Perfect agreement on dataset creation claims (C5-C7, C22, C70-C74). Both evaluations find the dataset contribution well-supported, with peer reviewers acknowledging it as 'an important contribution' and confirming 'comprehensive evaluation' without raising concerns about annotation quality or dataset characteristics.

Both address generalization testing claims (C53-C58) but with different confidence levels. OpenEval finds the generalization evidence well-supported with rigorous testing across diverse datasets. Peer reviewers acknowledge the comprehensive evaluation but express uncertainty due to concerns about baseline method performance (CellPose/StarDist underperforming Otsu), questioning whether baselines were optimally trained and thus undermining confidence in generalization claims.

Both evaluate performance comparison claims (C34-C47) but reach different conclusions. OpenEval finds comprehensive quantitative support with appropriate statistical testing. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting that 'Otsu thresholding alone' achieves results 'quite close' to WNet3D, questioning whether 'DL might not really be necessary,' and raising concerns about whether artifact removal was applied consistently to baselines, potentially affecting comparison validity.

Both address architectural modifications and method development (C29-C33, C77, C79-C81). OpenEval finds detailed architectural justifications well-supported with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers acknowledge the method as 'solid' without raising specific concerns about the architectural choices or training approach, though they focus more on method description than detailed validation.

Partial overlap on software accessibility claims. OpenEval R2 covers broader software development claims (C2-C4, C23, C51, C66-C69, C104-C105) finding them well-documented. Peer R7 focuses on subset (C4, C23, C51, C66-C69, C104-C105) and explicitly praises the 'Napari plugin' packaging, confirming accessibility and utility for laboratories without concerns.

Both address active learning workflow claims (C48-C50, C63). OpenEval finds the approach well-validated with statistical support demonstrating it addresses WNet3D's artifact limitation. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as part of comprehensive evaluation without specific concerns, noting the work offers 'possibility of eliminating time-consuming data labeling.'

Both evaluate performance metrics and hyperparameter tuning claims (C24-C25, C37-C40, plus C85-C86, C89-C92 in OpenEval). OpenEval finds rigorous quantitative validation with proper error estimates. Peer reviewers express strong uncertainty, noting CellPose and StarDist 'perform poorly' and 'underperform Otsu thresholding,' suggesting 'these methods were not trained in an optimal way' and stating results 'should by no means be taken as a fair assessment' of baseline capabilities.

Both address limitation claims (C48, C61-C62 overlap). OpenEval R13 covers broader limitations (C59-C62, C64-C65) finding honest assessment with appropriate citations. Peer R8 implicitly acknowledges these limitations through questions about artifact filtering, noting 'post-processing (or artifact removal) seems to have a substantial impact on accuracy,' which aligns with authors' stated limitations about artifact discrimination.

Minimal overlap (C9 only). OpenEval R8 evaluates main conclusion claims (C8-C9) as supported by comprehensive evidence. Peer R3 addresses performance comparisons including C9 but expresses uncertainty about whether the evidence truly supports the main claims given concerns about baseline performance and necessity of deep learning.

OpenEval evaluates baseline model descriptions (C82-C84) as accurately cited and appropriately contextualized. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these descriptive claims about SegResNet and other baseline architectures.
